free_tier.stated: 2 TB of AWS S3 cloud storage per dataset for individual users (10 TB for institutional subscribers). No published limit on the number of datasets. Standard (non-Open-Access) deposit is free; making it Open Access costs $1,950.

egress.terms: Gated: 'Must be IEEE Paid DataPort Subscriber to Access Files' on the free Standard tier. Reader pays $40/month individual, or the depositor pays $1,950 once for Open Access so anyone can download.

record.tooling: Web upload and DOI minting; no S3 API handed to the depositor despite the S3 backing store.
record.chaining: Allows datasets up to 2 TB for submission. Open access publication requires a $1,950 fee per dataset to remove paywall restrictions for readers.
record.limits_note: 2 TB/dataset; read behind subscriber paywall on the free tier; no private-dataset capability on the individual plan.
record.reliability_note: Allows free upload of datasets up to 2 TB, but requires paid subscriptions or individual download purchase fees for reader access.

record.provider: IEEE DataPort — Data Competition module (the free + public route)

free_tier.stated: 2 TB per dataset for individual users, 10 TB for Institutional Subscribers. The Data Competition submission type is listed as FREE and carries the same 2 TB / 10 TB ceilings. 'Dataset files may total up to 2 TB or 10 TB for Institutional Subscribers'. Competition files are stored in Amazon S3 and can be downloaded by any logged-in IEEE DataPort user, and 'If Competition has No Access Restrictions, no entry needs to be made in the Access Control List box and all users of IEEE DataPort that are logged in will have access.' That is the only route on this platform where storage is free AND reads are free, because the two paid routes both gate reads: Standard Dataset (free upload) exposes files only to subscribers, and Open Access Dataset costs $1,950 to make them public.

egress.terms: Free in the ordinary sense. Downloads are served from IEEE's own S3 bucket (ieee-dataport.s3.amazonaws.com, which correctly returns 403 to anonymous listing rather than 200-with-empty-body) and there is no egress meter on the participant side. Real ceiling is per-user concurrency, not bytes.

record.tooling: Two real paths. (1) S3: a subscriber gets an AWS access key/secret and the bucket is ieee-dataport, with the dataset path /ieee-dataport/<DATASET TYPE>/<USERID>/<DATASETID>. AWS CLI, boto3, s3cmd, Cyberduck, CrossFTP, S3 Browser all documented. (2) Competition participants read via the 'AWS S3' tab which reveals per-file S3 URIs plus a 'View AWS Security Credentials' dialog with the secret key. Undocumented but usable: the web upload form needs no subscription at all.
record.chaining: Datasets are unlimited per account and each carries an independent 2 TB ceiling, so the multiplier is datasets, not accounts. 10 datasets is 20 TB of nominal capacity on one free IEEE web account. Competition module can host several files per competition. Combining the two submission types on one account gives both a subscriber-upload path (S3) and a public-read path (competition).
record.limits_note: Write-gated + read-gated, and the gate differs by route. Standard Dataset: upload free, read requires IEEE DataPort subscription (~$480/yr). Open Access: read free to all, write costs $1,950 per dataset. Competition: both free, but the entry is framed as a time-limited challenge with start and end dates and 'Competitions must meet eligibility requirements and are not intended for general dataset publication'. Per-file cap is not stated; IEEE's own guidance is 'for large datasets, we recommend uploading a series of files that are 100 GB or less'. A soft 100 GB/file figure. Supported formats list is broad (zip, tar, 7z, iso, hdf5, parquet, avro, orc, mat, wav, mp4 …).
record.reliability_note: S3 bucket is real and correctly access-controlled (403, not a fake 200). IEEE may unpublish Standard Dataset entries whose files were never uploaded. Competition entries are time-bounded by design, so treat the competition route as a lease with a declared end date rather than an archive.

evidence.proved: 'Open Access Dataset $1,950'; 'Data Competition FREE … 2 TB Cloud Storage'. This single page proves all three routes and their prices.
